passages.text: Every friend will say, I also am his friend: But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is there not a grief in it even to death, When a companion and friend is turned to enmity?
passages.note: Betrayal by a friend; false friendship

passages.text: Forget not a friend in your soul; And be not unmindful of him in your riches.
passages.note: Remembering friends when life goes well

passages.text: And make the counsel of your heart to stand; For there is none more faithful to you than it. For a man’s soul is sometime wont to bring him tidings, More than seven watchmen that sit on high on a watch-tower.
passages.note: Trusting your own inner judgement in decisions

passages.text: Let reason be the beginning of every work, And let counsel go before every action.
My son, prove your soul in your life, And see what is evil for it, and give not that to it. For all things are not profitable for all men, Neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
passages.note: Knowing what is good for you; self-knowledge

passages.text: My son, let your tears fall over the dead, And as one that suffers grievously begin lamentation; And wind up his body according to his due, And neglect not his burial. Make bitter weeping, and make passionate wailing, And let your mourning be according to his desert, For one day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: And so be comforted for your sorrow.
passages.note: Permission to mourn a death fully

passages.text: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself. Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall your be; Yesterday for me, and today for you. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.
passages.note: Grief that lingers too long; letting the dead rest
